Hi Sasha —

Thanks for the worksheet — this is exactly the right starting point. Short answers up front then a proposed next step: 

- Lead times (high-level): Dedicated reserved pools (hosted) on H100 family: typically 6–8 weeks from commitment to predictable tranche capacity; Private (VPC or on-prem) installations: 10–16 weeks depending on hardware sourcing and network/ops windows. We can often accelerate early eval tranche to 2–3 weeks by using burst capacity in hosted.

- Tranche guidance (staircase): eval (10–15% of projected prod GPU units) -> pilot (30–40%) -> prod (remaining 45–60%). For your profiles I’d recommend an initial eval tranche sized for performance validation (16 x H100 or 32 x A100 equivalent) then a pilot tranche targeted at load validation (48 GPUs), and a 64–96 GPU steady-state pool for production depending on concurrency.

- MAP acceptance gates we usually include: model parity (latency + quality), cost per 1k tokens target, KV/prefix warmup behavior, SOC2 evidence checklist, and a canary traffic ramp plan.

Next step: can we book Tue 10:00 AM PT for a joint sizing call? I’ll bring a short GPU-sizing estimate (pdf) and loop in our solutions lead to confirm lead-time windows. I'll also send an internal note to ops/solutions for precise procurement windows.

I'll attach a quick estimate (gpu-sizing-estimate.pdf) to this thread.

Best,

Diego / team —

Thanks for the context. Below are concrete numbers we can include in the MAP draft plus recommended gating and fallback language. I’ve attached a short sizing PDF and flagged SOC2 artifacts we can share.

Lead times (calendar windows, US region):
- Hosted Dedicated (reserved H100 pool): 6–8 weeks from signed commitment to committed tranche availability. We can deliver an accelerated eval tranche (16 H100-equivalent) on hosted within 2–3 weeks using burst and preemptible capacity but we should state it as "subject to availability".
- Private VPC-managed (cloud-hosted in customer VPC): 8–12 weeks (depends on VPC peering, customer security review).
- On-prem managed installs: 12–16 weeks (hardware lead times + site readiness). Add a 4-week contingency for H100-specific procurement volatility.

Recommended tranche sizing (Ecosense profile):
- Eval (Week 0–3): 16 H100-equivalent GPUs — goal: latency parity, deterministic KV warmup, functional regressions.
- Pilot (Week 3–8): additional 32 GPUs (total 48) — goal: scale under representative concurrency, validate autoscaling and batching configs.
- Prod (Week 8+): scale to 64–80 GPUs steady-state; allow for a 20% buffer for early ramp.

Gating / MAP acceptance criteria to include in the document:
- Latency: P95 generator latency <= 120ms on pilot traffic profile with target batching config.
- Throughput: sustain 3M tokens/day across pilot with <2% error/timeout rate.
- Cost target: target tokens/unit cost threshold (insert dollar figure in MAP after finance run).
- Security: SOC2 artifact bundle (audit log samples, KMS config screenshot, retention policy summary) to be delivered at pilot handoff.
- Cutover plan: canary (1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with a rollback window and SLA-backed timeout.

Fallbacks and contingency language (suggested MAP text):
- If H100 lead times extend >12 weeks, Redwood to offer A100-equivalent pool as a trench with a documented performance delta and a one-time transition support plan.
- If SOC2 gating takes longer than 4 weeks, propose a temporary hosted-only pilot with strong data partitioning until on-prem readiness completes.

Timeline sketch (we can include calendar dates after the MAP draft call):
- Tue (call): confirm tranche sizes and finalize dates for EOD Mon MAP draft.
- Mon EOD: MAP draft delivered to Ecosense with milestone dates.
- Signed MAP -> Week 0: Eval tranche activation (2–3 weeks for accelerated hosted; 6–8 weeks for reserved).
- Week 3–8: Pilot tranche activation and SOC2 evidence handoff.
- Week 8+: Prod tranche scale and final acceptance.

Attachments to include with MAP: gpu-sizing-estimate.pdf, SOC2 artifact index (soc2-proof.zip).

I can draft the calendarized MAP language and milestone table; Diego, if you want I’ll prepare the commitable lead-time bullets and tranche wording for the customer-facing doc.
